I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so this is still the steadiest way for me to make use of the full year, match the local weather, and reduce market risk. I will finish the winter wheat already in the field, then follow it with summer maize on the same land. I would not spread myself into too many crops, because at my age I value a plan I can manage well with the labor and knowledge I have. Wheat and maize are familiar to me, the inputs are clear, irrigation timing is predictable, and I can sell both without much trouble.

For management, I will keep inputs moderate and practical. On wheat, I will focus on steady base fertilizer, one topdressing of nitrogen, irrigation at key stages, and a small number of pesticide sprays only when pressure is real. After wheat harvest, I will quickly prepare for summer maize so I do not lose moisture or the planting window. On maize, I will use hybrid seed for stable yield, give enough nitrogen for growth, add phosphorus and potassium as a base, and control weeds and insects with limited but timely applications. I will use rotary tillage because it is what I can manage efficiently between crops and it fits this rotation well.
